title: Add UNIQUE(character_id) to active_buffs, spell_slots and round_state so state upserts work
description:
State upserts fail at runtime: the DAL saves for active buffs, spell slots and the round counter use `ON CONFLICT(character_id) DO UPDATE`, but migration 003_state.sql creates active_buffs, spell_slots and round_state with only `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` and no UNIQUE constraint on character_id. SQLite rejects every such upsert with "ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint". Desired: each of the three tables holds at most one row per character, and the existing upserts work unchanged.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12, autonomous; supervisor-confirmed evidence)
- Fix in the schema, not in the queries: add a NEW migration (next number after 005); never edit 003.
- The migration first dedupes existing rows per character_id, keeping the row with the highest id (the latest write), then adds a UNIQUE index on character_id for active_buffs, spell_slots and round_state.
- Remove the 9 `t.Skip("bug: upserts use ON CONFLICT(character_id) ...")` DAL tests added by critical-518.3 (PR #13, branch feat/518.3-backfill-tests) in buffdal (7) and spelldal (2) tests. Hence blocked by critical-518.3: stack on that branch or start after it is merged.
- NOT in scope: the nat-1 / nat-20 `t.Skip("bug?: ...")` in combatsvc tests (separate rules decision, handled by the supervisor with the user).

## Current behaviour
SaveActiveBuffs, SaveSlots and SaveRoundNumber always fail, which breaks Activate / Dismiss / Trigger buff, Next Round, Cast spell and Reset slots. Reproduced live (dev-518-6): POST /api/spells/0/cast on a fresh DB -> 500 "save slots: upsert spell_slots: ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint".

## Key interfaces
- New migration file under the sqlite migrations dir, e.g. `006_state_unique_character.sql`: per table `DELETE FROM <t> WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT MAX(id) FROM <t> GROUP BY character_id);` then `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS <t>_character_id_uq ON <t>(character_id);`.
- The migration runner splits files on semicolons and executes statements one by one (no wrapping transaction), recording the file in schema_migrations only after all succeed: keep every statement idempotent and free of semicolons inside literals/comments.
- DAL query files (buffs.sql, spells.sql) and the BuffStore / spell-slot store ports stay unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New migration exists; 001-005 are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [ ] On a fresh DB, SaveActiveBuffs, SaveSlots and SaveRoundNumber succeed on first insert AND on a second save for the same character (row updated, still exactly one row).
- [ ] On a DB that already holds duplicate rows per character_id in any of the three tables, migrating keeps only the highest-id row per character and then creates the unique index (covered by a test that seeds duplicates before applying the new migration, or an equivalent migrate test).
- [ ] Re-running migrations on an already-migrated DB is a no-op (no error).
- [ ] The 9 buffdal/spelldal `t.Skip("bug: upserts use ON CONFLICT ...")` tests are un-skipped and pass.
- [ ] `just generate` run; any change in generated bob output (models/factory/queries) committed, and the CI generated-code check passes.
- [ ] Manual or HTTP-level check: POST /api/spells/0/cast on a fresh DB no longer returns 500.
- [ ] `just validate` passes.

## Tests
buffdal and spelldal DAL tests (the 9 un-skipped ones), plus a migration test for the dedupe-then-index path on pre-existing duplicates.

## Risky
Yes: migration on existing data (deletes duplicate rows) and buff / spell-slot / round-counter state semantics. Needs review per the workflow doc ("Migrations and DAL", "State integrity").

## Parallelism
Adds a migration touching active_buffs, spell_slots, round_state: do not run in parallel with another item adding a migration on those tables or changing bob generated output.

## Out of scope
- Changing the upsert queries or the store ports.
- The nat-1 / nat-20 combat skips.
- Merging the three tables or moving state into the characters table.
close_reason: Merged in PR #16

title: Decide fly.io hosting shape: access control, topology, backups
description:
Decisions needed before any fly.io work. The PRD says 'no authentication, Tailscale is the security boundary'; a public fly.io URL breaks that.

Questions for the user:
1. Access control: (a) shared-secret/basic auth at the edge, (b) fly private networking + WireGuard/Tailscale only (no public ingress), (c) real login. Recommendation: (a) or (b); the app has no user model and is a single-character personal tool.
2. Topology: one container where the Go API also serves the built web assets (simplest on fly: one machine, one volume), vs. separate api and nginx apps as in docker-compose. Recommendation: single container.
3. SQLite on fly: single machine + fly volume (no horizontal scale, which is fine). Backup via fly volume snapshots only, or Litestream to object storage? Recommendation: snapshots first, Litestream if the data matters.
4. Environments: production only, or also a staging app deployed from PRs?
5. Budget/region constraints.

Output: decisions recorded in this bead's notes and in docs/ (an ADR-style note), then the dependent beads are un-labelled needs-info.

title: Actor: remove db field, make pure value type
description:
Actor currently stores *sql.DB internally (actor.go:13), coupling the domain entity to persistence. Every Actor method (TakeDamage, GetHPState, ApplyBuff, etc.) is a thin wrapper that re-passes the same db to package-level functions.

Fix: remove the db field from Actor. LoadActor returns a plain struct with no DB reference. Callers (handlers) call the package-level domain functions directly — no Actor intermediary needed for persistence. Actor methods that are now pure (ApplyBuff, DismissBuff, TriggerBuff) keep their in-memory logic but drop the SaveActiveBuffs call; persistence is the caller's responsibility.

No new interface. No new abstraction. Just delete the field and its wrappers.

title: ResolveAttack: pre-aggregate modifiers, decouple from Actor
description:
engine.ResolveAttack (combat.go) reaches into actor.ActiveBuffs mid-calculation to apply modifiers. This means: (a) buff state can diverge between LoadActor and the call, (b) the function does hit resolution + damage + crit + buff aggregation in one 60-line god function with no seam.

Fix: introduce a CombatContext value (pre-computed attack bonus, damage formula, crit threshold, buff modifiers). ResolveAttack takes CombatContext + DiceRoller, returns CombatResult — pure function. The caller (handler or a thin builder) aggregates modifiers before calling. engine/buffs.go ApplyBuffModifiers already produces BuffModifiers; caller computes CombatContext from actor.Stats + BuffModifiers.

Benefit: engine is independently testable without a DB-backed actor. Buff aggregation changes don't touch combat.go.

Files: api/internal/engine/combat.go, api/internal/engine/buffs.go, api/internal/handlers/combat.go

title: Handler boilerplate: extract CharacterContext value struct
description:
Seven handler structs each repeat {DB *sql.DB, CharacterID int64}. This is accidental width — the same pair exists by coincidence, not design.

Fix: introduce a CharacterContext struct (db, characterID) that handlers embed. Constructor: NewCharacterContext(db, charID). Handlers become e.g. type HPHandler struct { CharacterContext }. main.go creates one CharacterContext and embeds it into all handlers.

No interface. No behavioral change. Eliminates the repeated field pair and makes main.go construction obvious.

title: SaveCategory: move from engine to domain, decouple HTTP from engine types
description:

title: Playwright e2e harness: just e2e on a throwaway stack, with smoke specs and docs
description:
Give agents a headless way to prove a UI acceptance criterion: a Playwright e2e harness behind `just e2e` that drives the real app (Go API + Vite) on a throwaway stack, saves screenshots for visual review and traces on failure. Lands before the dashboard redesign (critical-qki.6) so the redesign and every later UI item ship with specs.

User's words (2026-10-12): "i need you or your team to devise a proper UI testing strategy. probably using playwright."

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- Lands BEFORE qki.6 and blocks it (P1, mvp-saturday).
- Layers: Playwright e2e against the real API + screenshots as artifacts. No pixel-diff snapshot assertions, no component-test layer for now (vitest from qki.1 stays for units).
- Local only: no CI job yet (separate P3 item under critical-8g1). `just validate` unchanged; `just e2e` is a separate recipe.
- Mandatory per UI work item: Playwright specs covering its UI acceptance criteria, `just e2e` green, screenshot paths listed in the developer report.
- i18n: flow specs run in en; ONE fr smoke spec toggles to French and checks no raw keys are visible.
- Data: the repo's real `seeds/` + a fresh temp SQLite DB per spec file. Specs assert relative changes (HP drops by the damage entered), never hard-coded character values, so the qki.2 reseed does not break them.
- Selectors: getByRole/getByLabel with English accessible names first; `data-testid` only for non-semantic regions (HP value, log entries).
- Artifacts: HTML report, PNGs and traces in `web/e2e-results/` (gitignored); nothing binary committed. The supervisor relays PNG paths to the user.

## Current behaviour
Agents stop at typecheck/build (+ vitest units after qki.1); nobody can verify a panel headlessly; the supervisor tells the user "look at it yourself". The API does not serve the web build; Vite already reads `CRITICAL_API_URL` for its `/api` proxy; the API takes `CRITICAL_DSN`, `CRITICAL_SEEDS_DIR`, `CRITICAL_ADDR`. `just dev` binds fixed ports (:8080/:5173), so it can't be used by parallel worktrees.

## Key interfaces
- `just e2e` (from repo root): builds the API, installs/uses Playwright Chromium, runs the suite; any extra args pass through to `playwright test` (e.g. `just e2e smoke.spec.ts`). A `just e2e-install` (or equivalent first-run step) installs the browser.
- Playwright config in `web/` (specs under `web/e2e/`): Chromium only, viewport 1440x900, `trace: retain-on-failure`, output + HTML report under `web/e2e-results/`.
- A shared fixture that gives each spec file its own stack: API on a free port with a new temp DB under the OS temp dir and `CRITICAL_SEEDS_DIR` = repo `seeds/`, plus a Vite server on a free port whose `/api` proxy targets that API (the proxy target is fixed at Vite start, so either Vite per spec file too or an equivalent that keeps isolation). Processes and temp DBs cleaned up even on failure. Never touches `.dev/` or fixed ports, so two worktrees can run `just e2e` at the same time.
- A screenshot helper: `snap(page, name)` writes `web/e2e-results/screens/<spec>/<name>.png`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `just e2e` runs green from a fresh worktree after `npm ci` (+ the documented browser install step), with nothing else running.
- [ ] Two `just e2e` runs in parallel (e.g. two worktrees) don't collide: free ports, separate DBs.
- [ ] Smoke specs against the CURRENT dashboard: (a) app loads and shows the character's HP; (b) entering damage lowers current HP by exactly that amount without reload; (c) fr smoke: toggle to French, no raw i18n keys visible, screenshot saved.
- [ ] Each spec saves at least one PNG at 1440x900; a deliberately failing assertion leaves a trace zip in `web/e2e-results/`.
- [ ] `web/e2e-results/` and Playwright caches are gitignored; `just validate` does not run e2e and still passes (lint/typecheck include the e2e TS files without breaking).
- [ ] docs/agent-workflow.md updated: "Validation" (UI items must add/extend specs per UI acceptance flow and run `just e2e` green; list screenshot paths in the report), "Running the app for acceptance checks" (`just e2e`, artifacts location), "Review" (visual review uses the e2e screenshots); keep headings stable.
- [ ] docs/frontend.md gets a "Testing" section: layers, selector convention, relative assertions, en flows + one fr smoke, how to add a spec, where artifacts land.

## Tests
The smoke specs themselves; `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
CI job (separate item under critical-8g1); pixel-diff baselines; vitest component tests; specs for the redesign (qki.6 writes its own and may replace the smoke specs' selectors).

Blocked by critical-qki.1 (the fr smoke needs the language toggle; both edit web/package.json). Blocks critical-qki.6. Model: Sonnet (tooling, not a UI-heavy bead). Not risky per the review triggers.

title: Action log: one append-only log of table actions with audited amend/void
description:
One append-only action log records every table action and lets the user amend or void any entry; it becomes the HP ledger and the combat log. Backend + API only; the redesign item builds the UI on it.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- "damage/healing ledger with good ui. should be able to amend/correct a mistake" (user).
- One action log for all actions (HP change, cast, buff change, Next Round, attack, item use), not per-feature undo.
- Each entry stores before/after snapshots of the state it changed (buffs, slots, round, counters). Voiding an entry restores its "before" state when no later non-voided entry changed the same state; otherwise the void is refused with a clear error (or the user voids the later one first).
- Corrections are audited: amend/void are new events pointing at the original; history shows "amended"/"voided". No in-place edits.

## Current behaviour
hp_events ledger with append + "undo last" only; buffs/slots/round are JSON state rows overwritten in place, no history; nothing records attacks or casts.

## Key interfaces
- Action entry: id, character_id, round, kind (hp_change | cast | buff_change | round_advance | attack | item_use | ...), summary payload (JSON, e.g. full RollResult for attacks), before/after state snapshots, created_at, status derived from correction events.
- Correction event: target action id, kind amend|void, new payload for amend (amend on HP changes: amount and source).
- A domain port other services use to record an action atomically with their state write (same transaction).
- Current HP = SUM of effective HP deltas (amended value, voided = 0), still computed in SQL.
- REST: `GET /api/log` (newest first, with correction status), `POST /api/log/{id}/amend`, `POST /api/log/{id}/void`; existing `POST /api/hp/event` now writes through the log; `/api/hp/undo` = void of the last HP entry.
- Existing hp_events data migrated (new migration file, never edit an applied one).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] HP damage/heal recorded as log entries; amend changes current HP and keeps the original visible; void removes its effect.
- [ ] Voiding an entry with snapshots restores the before state; voiding when a later entry changed the same state is refused with `{"error": ...}`.
- [ ] Record + state write are one transaction (test with a failing DAL).
- [ ] Migration applies on an existing dev DB with hp_events data; totals unchanged.
- [ ] Service and DAL tests per docs/backend.md; `just generate` and `just mocks` run; `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
Recording casts, rounds, buffs, attacks, items (each feature item plugs into this port); the UI.

Risky: migration + ledger/state semantics.

title: Extract Wizard spell effects into a seed (one-off, agent-run)
description:
One-off, agent-run extraction of structured effects for Wizard spells from the spell database text into a seed file the rules engine can use.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- "Parse all spells" was refined by the user to: a one-off extraction run by an agent, Wizard list only (bards cast wizard spells), writing a seed with a confidence flag per spell. No runtime text parsing.

## Current behaviour

## Key interfaces
seeds/spell_effects.json (+ a JSON schema), one entry per Wizard spell keyed by the spell id/name used in spells.json:
- kind: buff | damage | utility
- buff: modifiers (to_hit, damage, ac, save, str_set/str_bonus, spells_buff multiplier, weapon_buff, multiplier, charges e.g. Stoneskin layers / Mirror Images), target (self/other), duration formula in rounds as a function of caster level (e.g. "1/level", "3+1/level", "2d4"), charges formula (e.g. Stoneskin "1d4 + level/2").
- damage: dice formula by caster level with cap (e.g. Fireball "1d6/level, max 10d6"), save type and effect (half/negates/none).
- confidence: high | low, and a note for low ones.
A loader + validator in Go that rejects malformed formulas at startup.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every Wizard spell in spells.json has an entry; spellbook spells (Strength, Improved Strength, Haste, Enlarge, Stoneskin, Mirror Image, Fireball, Lightning Bolt, Cone of Cold, Magic Missile, Chromatic Orb, Melf's Acid Arrow, Flame Arrow, Protection from Evil, Slow, Dispel Magic, Polymorph Self, Improved Invisibility, ...) are `high`.
- [ ] Strength (wizard 2nd level) encodes the rogue-class bonus per PHB (+1d6 STR for rogues/bards); Enlarge encodes the damage multiplier.
- [ ] Loader test: the repo seed validates; a malformed formula fails startup with a clear error.
- [ ] A short report (in the PR body) listing low-confidence spells.
- [ ] `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
Applying effects at cast time (cast item); priest spells; French texts.

Not blocked; seeds + a loader package, parallel-safe with the i18n and character-seed items.

title: Resolve attacks with real weapons, ammo and full AD&D 2.5 modifiers
description:
Attack resolution with the Bard's real weapons and correct AD&D 2.5 modifiers, every one shown in the breakdown and recorded in the action log.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- No special natural rolls: nat 1 is not an auto-miss, nat 20 is not an auto-hit. Delete the skipped TestResolveAttack_NaturalRolls and add a test that proves plain THAC0 math at 1 and 20.
- Crit: keep the house rule (D20 - D100 >= roll needed -> crit); multiplier stays x2, labelled "placeholder" in the breakdown until the crit-table item lands.
- Power Gem: its weapon effects (+5, x2) apply only while effective STR is 18.
- Effective STR = base STR (12) modified by active STR buffs (Strength, Improved Strength, possibly cast by other players).

## Current behaviour
STR>=18 hard-codes +1 hit/+2 dmg; no magic weapon bonus, no DEX for missiles, no target size, no situational modifier, buffs add nothing to hit; crit x2 hard-coded.

## Key interfaces
- Request: weapon id, ammo item id (missile weapons), target AC, target size (S/M | L), situational modifier (signed int + label, optional).
- To-hit: THAC0 13; STR hit adj (melee, from effective STR via the PHB table); DEX missile adj (missile); weapon magic; ammo magic (missile; PHB rule for magic bow + magic arrow); buff to-hit; situational. Each a Modifier{source,value}.
- Damage: weapon die by target size; formula per docs/backend.md ((Base x SpellsBuff) + WeaponBuff) x Multipliers + StrengthBonus, plus weapon/ammo magic damage and buff damage as listed modifiers; STR damage adj only for melee (and per PHB for bows: none).
- Buff effects gain to_hit and damage fields; aggregation uses effective STR (MinStr gating unchanged in meaning).
- Missile attack decrements the chosen ammo (via the items port); the attack is recorded in the action log with the full RollResult and ammo snapshot.
- Attack tab in the round screen: weapon, ammo, target AC, size, situational modifier, result card.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Table-driven tests for: long sword +2 vs AC 5 at STR 12 and STR 18; short bow +2 with +3 arrow (DEX 17); bastard sword 2H vs L; buff to-hit; situational modifier; Power Gem active at STR 18 and ignored at STR 17; crit flagged "placeholder x2".
- [ ] Every modifier appears in RollResult.Modifiers / damage breakdown; web/src/types matches Go.
- [ ] Voiding an attack in the log restores the arrow count.
- [ ] `just validate` green.
- [ ] Playwright specs (per critical-qki.16 conventions) cover this item's UI acceptance criteria; `just e2e` green; screenshot paths listed in the report. (added 2026-10-12, UI testing triage)

## Out of scope
Real crit table; POCT crit systems; Gaia protections; Power Gem form choice (thunder hammer etc.).

Risky: rules math. Opus. Blocked by character seed (STR/DEX tables), weapons & items, and the round screen. Touches buffsvc like the buffs item: not parallel with it.

title: Buffs that matter: logged edits, undoable Next Round, charge buffs, effective STR
description:
Buffs that matter: logged, editable, undoable, with charge buffs for Stoneskin and Mirror Images and STR-changing buffs.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- Correctable: buff edits (remaining rounds/charges) and Next Round (step back restores durations) via the action log snapshots.
- Stoneskin layers and Mirror Images must work on Saturday: charge buffs with a one-tap "absorbed a hit" that decrements.
- Buffs may be cast on the Bard by other players; STR buffs (Strength, Improved Strength) change effective STR, which gates the Power Gem.

## Current behaviour
Free-form buff builder (one effect key/value); Next Round decrements durations in a transaction but nothing is logged; no edit; trigger exists for charge buffs; no STR or to-hit/AC effects.

## Key interfaces
- Buff effects extended with str_set / str_bonus and ac (to_hit/damage are added by the attack item; coordinate, don't duplicate).
- `GetEffectiveStr(characterID)` (domain, used by combat and gating).
- `PATCH /api/buffs/{id}` (remaining duration/charges), trigger, dismiss, activate and Next Round all write an action log entry with before/after snapshot; voiding restores.
- Buffs strip in the round screen: name, remaining rounds/charges as Badge, edit, dismiss, "absorbed" for charge buffs; expiry toast on Next Round.
- A manual buff form remains for things not in the spell effects seed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Next Round then void -> round number and durations restored; buffs that expired come back.
- [ ] Editing a buff's remaining rounds is logged and voidable.
- [ ] Stoneskin with N layers: each "absorbed" decrements; at 0 the buff ends; voidable.
- [ ] Effective STR with a Strength buff active reaches 18 -> Power Gem effects aggregate; drops when it expires.

- [ ] Playwright specs (per critical-qki.16 conventions) cover this item's UI acceptance criteria; `just e2e` green; screenshot paths listed in the report. (added 2026-10-12, UI testing triage)

Applying buffs from spell casts (cast item); AC display beyond the buff list.

Not risky under this epic's relaxed review (user QAs), though it is state semantics. Opus. Blocked by the action log and the round screen. Touches buffsvc like the attack item: not parallel with it.

title: Prepare today's spells from the spellbook within PHB Bard limits
description:
The user prepares today's spells from the Bard's spellbook, limited per spell level by the PHB Bard table for the character's level.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- "selecting spells for the day respecting limits" (user). Limits come from the PHB Bard table by level (level 15: 3/3/3/3/2), no per-character override.
- Spell names displayed via i18n keys (fr names for the spellbook spells).

Prepared spells are fixed in seeds/character.json; slots are a JSON list; cast only flags `used`.

- Spellbook: the spells the Bard knows (from the sheet, Dashboard column A and tab Parchemins), linked to the spell database id; fr names added to the `spells` i18n namespace.
- Preparation: `PUT /api/spells/prepared` with spell ids (duplicates allowed, e.g. Mirror Image x2); refuses when a level exceeds BardSpellsPerDay(level) or a spell is not in the spellbook. Long rest resets used flags and keeps the preparation.
- Preparation is recorded in the action log.
- Spells tab in the round screen: per level, remaining/total, prepared list with Cast (cast effects are a separate item), "Prepare" editor that searches the spellbook.

- [ ] Spellbook matches the sheet (check the French->English mapping in the PR body for the user to review).
